newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen parliament speaker rules out Israel ties.
newsitem.headline: Yemen parliament speaker rules out Israel ties.

text.p: Yemen's Islamist parliament speaker said on Sunday that his country would be the last to consider normalising ties with Israel.

Sheikh Abdullah bin Hussein al-Ahmar, head of the Islah party which ruled as the junior coalition partner in the outgoing government, said solving Yemen's decades-old border row with Saudi Arabia was the Arab state's top priority.

"Yemen is the last country to think of normalising relations with Israel," he told reporters after the 301-seat parliament held its first session after last month's general elections. Parliament re-elected Ahmar as speaker earlier on Sunday.
Yemen in February dismissed Israeli talk of secret contacts between the two countries as "mere fabrication" and denied it was setting up ties with the Jewish state.

Israel has a foothold in the Gulf with trade missions in Oman and Qatar. But Oman and Qatar have said they had frozen contacts with Israel because of what they considered hardline Israeli policies towards Palestinians.
"Settling the Yemeni-Saudi border dispute is at the centre of concern on all Yemeni levels -- the people, the leadership and parliament," Ahmar said. "This is of vital interest for the two peoples."
Saudi Arabian and Yemeni delegates are due to meet in Saudi in June to discuss border demarcation between the oil-rich kingdom and its impoverished neighbour.
Yemen has hinted it might resort to international arbitration if talks with Riyadh failed to settle the 61-year-old conflict.
